title: Better first one-to-ones
subtitle: A little less advice. A better conversation.
outcome: Ask an open question, listen before advising, and agree a clear next step.
fictional: A fictional learning example · Northstar Services

topics.title: Start with curiosity
topics.headline: You do not need all the answers.
topics.summary: Your first one-to-one is a chance to understand someone’s work, not prove that you know everything.
topics.detail: Think of a colleague you will speak with this week. What would you like to understand about their work? Keep that person in mind as you explore the board.
topics.prompt: What might you learn if you ask before you advise?

topics.title: Ask
topics.headline: Open the conversation.
topics.summary: Ask one open question about the colleague’s work. Leave room for an answer you did not expect.
topics.detail: An open question helps the colleague describe what matters to them. A leading question embeds your own answer before they have had a chance to explain.
topics.prompt: Try a question beginning with “What…” or “How…”.

topics.title: Listen
topics.headline: Understand before you solve.
topics.summary: Let them finish. Reflect back what you heard. Check whether you understood it.
topics.detail: Reflection is a check, not a diagnosis. If you have misunderstood, let the colleague correct you before exploring a solution.
topics.prompt: What would you say to check your understanding?

topics.title: Agree
topics.headline: Make the next step clear.
topics.summary: Decide one next action together. Name the action, its owner and the follow-up date.
topics.detail: “We should communicate better” is hard to follow up. Agree what someone will actually do and when you will check whether it helped.
topics.prompt: Can both people say what will happen next?

topics.title: Meet Sam
topics.headline: What would you say next?
topics.summary: “Every shift the priorities change. I feel like I am always behind.”
topics.detail: Choose the strongest opening for this fictional situation. The explanation matters more than getting a letter right.

choices.text: Try making a better to-do list.
choices.feedback: Advice arrives before you understand the work. Ask what is happening first.

choices.text: Which change has made the biggest difference this week?
choices.feedback: This invites a concrete example without assuming the cause. Now listen and reflect back what you heard.

choices.text: We are all busy; it will settle down.
choices.feedback: This closes the conversation. Acknowledge the concern and ask an open question.

topics.title: Make it yours
topics.headline: Three minutes. One better conversation.
topics.summary: Work in pairs: one manager, one Sam. Rehearse the conversation, then keep one next action.
topics.detail: Use the remaining minute to reflect and write your own next action. If working alone, say your opening and reflection aloud, then write the action you would agree.
topics.prompt: Did you ask, listen and agree? What will you do next?
